data.raw_text: On the night of 6 Jan 1995, firefighters responded to a chemical fire in room 603 of the Doña Josefa apartment complex in Manila, Philippines. After a confrontation with two suspicious men who attempted to block their entry, the firefighters notified police. In the early morning hours of 7 Jan, police raided the apartment. Along with a manual in Arabic on constructing bombs using liquids, the police found chemicals, timers, fuses, multiple counterfeit passports, and priest’s clothing. The most valuable piece of evidence were disks and a computer belonging to Ramzi Yousef, the man responsible for the 1993 World Trade Center bombing. Floppy disks next to the computer contained the plan for operation “Bojinka,” a plot to destroy 12 U.S. bound flights over the Pacific scheduled for 21 Jan and the assassination of Pope John Paul II in the Philippines using an SVEST concealed by priest’s garments scheduled for 15 Jan. It was later revealed that the plan also included flying a plane into CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia. Yousef had planned Bojinka along with his uncle, Khalid Sheikh Mohammed. He had successfully tested bombs in Cebu, in Manila, and on Philippine Airlines Flight 434killing one passenger on 11 Dec in an act that almost brought down the aircraft. Ramzi Yousef was captured in Islamabad by Pakistani ISI and members of the U.S. Diplomatic Security Service on 7 Feb 1995. Yousef is currently serving two life sentences plus 240 years in Supermax Prison ADX Florence in Colorado in solitary confinement. Bojinka taught Khalid Sheikh Mohammed that liquid chemical bombs were susceptible to discovery. His next attack would use the airplanes themselves; he would turn them into instruments of terror. The lessons of Bojinka formed the basis for the attacks of 11 Sept 2001. He was captured on 1 Mar 2003 in Rawalpindi, Pakistan in a joint ISI, DSS, and CIA operation. He currently resides in the Guantanamo Bay detention facility as legal proceedings continue.
